text:
maria (PM): Heads up — proposing a new "reserved buffer" product: SLA-backed headroom that holds a small guaranteed pool for committed customers and auto-falls back to cheaper variants when exhausted. want quick sync on launch criteria and ops playbook.

alex (Eng): sounds useful for customers with spiky traffic. what's target headroom size? percentage or token model?

maria (PM): thinking 10% of committed qps or a token bucket equal to 30 minutes of peak for the tier, whichever is smaller. open to alternatives. focus is deterministic latency SLO at normal peak.

chris (Infra): technical constraints: keeping dedicated reserved nodes idle for just headroom is expensive. prefer ephemeral warm lanes with fast preemptible fallback. we can implement prefix-KV pinning + fast warmup.

lee (SRE): operational concerns: preemption fallback must be seamless. require canary failover plan + automated routing policy. need playbook for noisy tenants.

sam (Finance): cost model question: do we charge a buffer fee vs bake into reserved monthly? two options: small monthly buffer surcharge (predictable) or usage-billed when buffer used. prefer predictable surcharge for revenue.

anya (Legal): customers will ask for explicit SLA language. we need clear failure modes and credits. also data residency & logging requirements for private deployments.

maria (PM): draft launch acceptance criteria (proposal):
- SLO: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms under committed baseline + buffer usage.
- Failover correctness: when buffer exhausted, fallback to queued low-cost model or spillover region with <500ms added tail-latency for 99% requests.
- Billing: buffer included in reservation tier by default, with opt-out usage-billing for a-la-carte. pricing rec to finance due today.
- Observability: per-tenant buffer usage metric, headroom remaining, failover count, and a daily digest.
- Safety: rollback if failover causes >=1% increase in error-rate sustained 5m or >=500 requests failed in 10m.

chris (Infra): implementation notes:
- add a BufferManager service to track token buckets per-reservation.
- smart routing ties to existing smart routing layer, policy: "reserved->buffer->fallback".
- KV cache prewarm: keep smallest KV pages pinned when buffer is allocated.

alex (Eng): quick config sketch (for ops/devs):
```
reserved_buffer: 
  allocation_mode: percent # or token
  percent: 10
  token_minutes: 30
  fallback_policy: spill_region
  billing: surcharge_monthly | usage_on_use
  rollback_triggers:
    error_rate_spike: 1pct_5m
    latency_increase: p99_over_500ms_5m
```

lee (SRE): runbook items:
- Pre-launch: chaos test where we artificially exhaust buffer and validate fallback loop.
- Canary: 1% of customers in staged region for 48h, monitor headroom metrics + latency + errors.
- Escalation: if rollback trigger hits, auto-route new requests to fallback and fire page to oncall + PM.

maria (PM): launch checklist (MVP):
- Implementation of BufferManager + routing (ENG)
- Pricing recommendation from Finance (SAM)
- SLA wording + credits (ANYA)
- Observability dashboard + alerts (SRE)
- Docs + SDK tuning guide (DevEx)
- Legal sign-off for private deployments

sam (Finance): rough pricing proposal: base reservation price + 12% buffer surcharge for tier-1; usage billing path: $X per minute of buffer consumed. will model and share numbers tomorrow.

anya (Legal): will draft SLA clause that calls out "buffer exhaustion" as a defined failure mode with specific credit caps. also require customer opt-in for cross-region fallback.

alex (Eng): question on preemption semantics: when buffer is reclaimed (preempt), do we evict KV pages or let them be reclaimed lazily? eviction spike could hurt latency.

chris (Infra): prefer soft-eviction: mark pages reclaimable but allow LRU grace for N minutes. that reduces thundering-warm-up. need a small warm-pool reserved per-tenant.

lee (SRE): monitoring thresholds to add: sustained buffer-utilization > 80% for 30m => auto-notify capacity team; >95% => consider temporary uplift or customer outreach.

maria (PM): rollout timeline proposal:
- Week 0-2: design and pricing finalize
- Week 3-6: engineering sprint (BufferManager + routing + basic metrics)
- Week 7: internal canary + chaos tests
- Week 8-9: customer pilot (2-3 customers)
- Week 10: GA if pilot metrics pass

alex (Eng): dependency note: needs infra change to metric ingestion for per-tenant buffer usage. raising ticket to eng-infra.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-4821 "per-tenant buffer metrics ingestion" assigned to eng-infra.

lee (SRE): anyone object to adding a hard limit on pilot customers (max 3) to keep blast radius small?

sam (Finance): agree. also require pilot customers sign updated contract with buffer terms.

maria (PM): agreed. next steps: alex + chris to produce a short spec doc for BufferManager by EOD Wed; sam to post pricing sketch; anya to draft SLA clause. will schedule 30m sync Thu morning.

alex (Eng): ack, will post spec in #product-docs and link here.

chris (Infra): ack. I'll start prototypes for soft-eviction logic.

lee (SRE): will create canary test checklist and chaos plan.

maria (PM): thanks everyone :thumbsup: — keeping this thread as the single source for launch decisions.
